text:
B: Hi, can you hear me okay?
A: Er, yeah. Fine, yeah.
B: Great. I'm Gareth, by the way.
A: Oh. Erm, so am I, actually.
B: No way. Two Gareths. That's going to confuse whoever's typing this up, yeah?
A: Probably, aye.
B: So where are you, Gareth?
A: Wrexham.
B: Proper Welsh Gareth, then. I'm in Chelmsford, so Essex. Mine was just my mum liking the name, I think. What do you do for work?
A: Erm, admin. Transport office at a building supplies place. Book the deliveries in, dispatch spreadsheet, that sort of thing.
B: Right. So logistics, basically. That's not a million miles off what I do, to be honest. I'm a travel consultant, tailor-made trips, so a lot of my day is transfer times, flight connections, making sure the driver's actually at the airport when the client lands. When it works nobody notices, and when it doesn't, it's your fault, you know?
A: Yeah. Yeah, that's about right.
B: Where do you tend to go on holiday, then? Occupational hazard, I always ask.
A: Erm, caravan near Abersoch, mostly. And Tenerife every couple of years. The wife books it.
B: Tenerife's alright. Have you ever done the north of the island? Up round Teide, away from the resorts, it's a completely different place.
A: No. We sort of just stay by the pool, you know.
B: Fair enough. Nothing wrong with that. Honestly, half my clients would be better off by a pool than doing the itinerary they've asked me for.
A: Where's the, er, picture behind you?
B: Kyoto. I took it, actually. I've been to Japan five times. I'm learning Japanese at the moment, with a tutor once a week, which is humbling, I'll be honest.
A: Bloody hell. Fair play.
B: It's slow going. What do you do outside work?
A: Erm, football, mainly. Wrexham. Watch them on the telly, go a few times a season with my dad. Bit of PlayStation with my mates.
B: Wrexham's had a bit of a moment, hasn't it, with the Hollywood owners. I'll be straight with you, I'm not really a football person. Formula One's more my thing.
A: Right. Don't really watch that.
B: No, most people find it boring. I run as well. Training for a marathon, trying to get under three and a half hours.
A: Not for me, that. I walk the dog round the block, that's about it.
B: That's your photo, the dog bed? What have you got?
A: Staffy. Dot. She chewed through the telly remote cable last week.
B: Ha. That's the downside of a dog, I guess. I'm in a flat, so it's not really an option, and I'm away too much anyway.
A: Yeah, she'd not like that. She sulks if we're out a whole day.
B: Does she? Bit mardy, then.
A: Bit, yeah. She gets over it if you give her a sausage.
B: Doesn't everyone. So, nine years in the same job, did you say, or...
